pressure.title: Air changes, dilution and pressurisation
pressure.description: Ventilation removes heat and dilutes contaminants: rooms are designed for an air-change rate (e.g. ≈ 6–12 per hour, or by heat load Q = P / (ρ·cp·ΔT)) and, in hazardous areas, enough dilution to keep gas below a fraction of its LEL. Supply slightly exceeding exhaust keeps electrical and control rooms at positive pressure (≈ 25–50 Pa) so dust and flammable gas cannot enter; low-level exhaust removes heavier-than-air vapours. Fire dampers close on fire alarm.

script.narration: This module introduces the Ventilation System.
An industrial ventilation system supplies filtered, conditioned air to a room and exhausts contaminated air, removing heat and diluting gases.
Supply slightly exceeding exhaust keeps electrical and control rooms at positive pressure so dust and flammable gas cannot enter; low-level exhaust removes heavy vapours.
Typical applications include electrical / control rooms, analyser houses, battery rooms; process buildings, workshops and compressor houses.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Supply Fan, Exhaust Fan Impeller.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Ventilation System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Ventilation System.
Check room ΔP and temperature.
Change filters on ΔP.
Service fans, coils, dampers.
Watch for loss of pressurisation: alarm. Common cause: fan trip, door open.
Watch for overheating: high room temperature. Common cause: blocked filter, coil fouled.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
